title: A sub-plan's notes are private
idea: TOOL. Introduce scope gently: a variable created INSIDE a function is the function's own private note. Code outside cannot see it. Shown with predictable behaviour.

exercises.prompt: A sub-plan sometimes makes a helper variable while it works. Who can see that variable?
options: Only the code inside that sub-plan
exercises.explanation: A variable made inside a function is private to that function — like a note it keeps to itself while working.

exercises.prompt:
Read:

def greet():
    message = 7
    print(message)

greet()

What prints?
exercises.explanation: Inside greet, message is 7 and gets printed. The variable works fine INSIDE the function.

exercises.prompt:
Now outside the function:

def greet():
    message = 7

greet()
print(message)

What happens?
options: An error — message is not known outside greet
exercises.explanation: message lived only inside greet. Out here the name is unknown, so Python errors. That is scope.

exercises.prompt: A variable created inside a function keeps existing after the function finishes.
exercises.explanation: No — the function's private notes are forgotten when it ends. Use return to hand a value back instead.

exercises.prompt: Why does a function keep its helper variables private?
options: So different sub-plans can use the same name without clashing
exercises.explanation: Privacy means two functions can both use 'total' without stepping on each other. Each has its own.

exercises.prompt: Match the idea to its meaning.

pairs.right: A note only the function can see
The proper way to hand a value OUT
Where a name can be seen

exercises.explanation: A private variable is invisible outside; return is how you share a result; scope is the region where a name exists.

exercises.prompt:
Predict:

def box():
    side = 4
    return side * side

print(box())
exercises.explanation: Inside box, side is 4 and box returns 16. We print the RETURNED value, not the private 'side'.

exercises.prompt: If you want a value a function made, what should the function do?
options: hope you can read its private variable
exercises.explanation: return is the doorway out. Reaching for the private variable directly will not work.

exercises.prompt: print(side) placed after a call to box() (where side is defined inside box) will show 4.
exercises.explanation: It errors — side is private to box. Only box can see it.

exercises.prompt: The one big idea of this lesson:
options: Variables made inside a function are private to it; use return to share a result
exercises.explanation: A sub-plan's working notes stay inside. To get a value out, hand it back with return.
